reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports that trace interstitials promote phase segregation and that this depletion causes softening, but it does not provide any evidence linking this softening to a loss of toughness or increased brittleness under mechanical loading, which is a key premise of the hypothesis.
premises: Trace interstitials (O, N) promote phase segregation during thermal aging at 700°C
Phase segregation depletes solute interstitials from the matrix
Depletion of interstitials causes progressive softening
Softening leads to loss of toughness and increased brittleness under mechanical loading
